text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Little-known opposition National Democratic Party of Kenya chairman Stephen Omondi says he is ready to step down in favour of former member of parliament Raila Odinga.

- In what is probably the easiest theft of its magnitude in the East African region, a man walks into the strongroom of Kenya Airfreight Handling Limited and leaves with 54.7 million shillings ($1 million).
- Schools in the north eastern area of Samburu may not open this term owing to tension prevailing in the area after killing of the District Commissioner and two army pilots a month ago.
- Patients will now pay double for a bed at the Kenyatta National Hospital and three times more for wound dressing and treatment of broken limbs, among other shocking new charges.

- FORD-Asili National Treasurer Haroun ole Lempaka, a respected Maasai community leader is urged to decamp from the opposition and seek the Narok North parliamentary seat through the ruling party KANU party.
- FORD-Kenya Luo leaders claim Raila Odinga has given himself the powers of the "Luo spokesman", a title they say he is not qualified to hold.
- The Nairobi Provincial Commissioner moves swiftly to investigate the problems that led to the closure of Mukuru Community Centre School in a Nairobi slum district.

- Kenya's Chief Justice orders that a former army captain Geoffrey Ngengi, in a group of three people including dissident Koigi wa Wamwere sentenced to four-years in jail for robbery, be admitted to Nairobi Hospital for treatment immediately.
